topics.name: Christianity
topics.kicker: World’s largest religion · Based on the life and teachings of Jesus
topics.briefing: Christianity grew from a small group of Jesus’s followers in the 1st century CE into the world’s largest religion, practiced by more than two billion people. Christians believe that Jesus of Nazareth is the Son of God, that he was crucified in Jerusalem, and that he rose from the dead, which they celebrate at Easter. Its holy book, the Bible, joins the Old Testament to the New Testament, which tells of Jesus and his first followers.
topics.answerHtml: Christianity (accept word forms like Christians; do not accept a single branch such as “Catholicism” or “Protestantism”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Around 112 CE, Pliny the Younger wrote to the emperor Trajan [“TRAY-jun”] asking how to deal with followers of this religion, who met before dawn to sing hymns “to Christ as to a god.” The historian Tacitus wrote that Nero had blamed its followers for the Great Fire of Rome in 64 CE.
tossups.r: Its early missionaries included the apostle Paul. For 10 points, name this religion that grew out of the teachings of Jesus of Nazareth.

tossups.p: Before the Battle of the Milvian Bridge in 312 CE, Constantine reportedly had his soldiers mark their shields with the Chi-Rho [“KY-roh”], a symbol made from the first two Greek letters of “Christ.” The next year, the Edict of Milan allowed this religion to be practiced freely across the Roman Empire.
tossups.r: Constantine himself was baptized shortly before he died. For 10 points, name this religion whose followers believe Jesus is the Son of God.

tossups.p: At a council called by Constantine in 325 CE, bishops condemned Arius [“AIR-ee-us”], who taught that the Son had been created by the Father, and declared the Son to be “of the same substance” as the Father. That Council of Nicaea [“ny-SEE-uh”] produced the first version of a creed still recited in many of this religion’s churches.
tossups.r: That creed is the Nicene Creed. For 10 points, name this religion whose major churches teach the Trinity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

tossups.p: In 1054, a papal legate and the patriarch Michael Cerularius [“seh-roo-LAIR-ee-us”] excommunicated each other in Constantinople, a break later seen as the start of a split within this religion. Disputes over the pope’s authority and over adding the word filioque [“fil-ee-OH-kway”], meaning “and the Son,” to a creed helped cause that Great Schism.
tossups.r: It divided the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches. For 10 points, name this religion founded on the teachings of Jesus.

tossups.p: The Council of Trent, which met from 1545 to 1563, and a new order called the Jesuits led a Catholic response to a movement that split this religion in Western Europe. That movement began in 1517, when Martin Luther posted his Ninety-five Theses.
tossups.r: It produced Protestant churches such as the Lutherans. For 10 points, name this religion whose main branches are Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant.

tossups.p: Early followers of this religion used a fish symbol because the Greek word for “fish,” ichthys [“IK-thees”], could be read as an acronym for “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior.” According to the Acts of the Apostles, its believers first got their name in the city of Antioch.
tossups.r: The missionary Paul spread it among non-Jews around the Mediterranean. For 10 points, name this religion whose best-known symbol is the cross.

tossups.p: Tradition says that Gregory the Illuminator converted King Tiridates [“tir-ih-DAY-teez”] III, making Armenia in 301 CE the first kingdom to adopt this religion as its official faith. In Africa, the kingdom of Aksum [“AHK-soom”] adopted it under King Ezana in the 300s.
tossups.r: In 380, the emperor Theodosius I made it the official religion of the Roman Empire. For 10 points, name this religion based on the teachings of Jesus.

tossups.p: The Catholic and Orthodox branches of this religion count seven sacraments, including confirmation and the anointing of the sick, while most Protestant churches count only two. In one of those rites, believers share bread and wine, as Jesus did with his disciples at the Last Supper.
tossups.r: That rite is called the Eucharist, or Holy Communion. For 10 points, name this religion whose followers believe Jesus rose from the dead on Easter.

tossups.p: In Western churches, this religion’s most important holiday usually falls on the first Sunday after the first full moon of spring. It comes after a season of about forty days of prayer and fasting called Lent, which begins on Ash Wednesday, and the week before it includes Palm Sunday and Good Friday.
tossups.r: That holiday, Easter, celebrates the day its followers believe Jesus rose from the dead. For 10 points, name this religion.

tossups.p: Many Orthodox churches of this religion celebrate one of its major holidays on January 7, because they follow the older Julian calendar. Western churches celebrate that holiday on December 25 after a season of preparation called Advent, and twelve days later they mark Epiphany, which recalls the visit of the Magi.
tossups.r: That holiday, Christmas, celebrates the birth of Jesus, which the Gospels of Matthew and Luke place in Bethlehem. For 10 points, name this religion.

tossups.p: The Second Vatican Council, which met from 1962 to 1965, allowed the Catholic branch of this religion to celebrate Mass in local languages instead of Latin. Many centuries earlier, Saint Jerome translated its scriptures into Latin in a version called the Vulgate.
tossups.r: Its holy book, the Bible, has an Old Testament and a New Testament. For 10 points, name this religion.

tossups.p: At the end of the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus tells his followers to make disciples of all nations, baptizing them “in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” Most branches of this religion teach that those three persons form one God, the Trinity.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this religion whose followers believe that Jesus rose from the dead on the third day after he was crucified.

tossups.p: In the Sermon on the Mount, this religion’s central figure blesses the meek, the merciful, and the peacemakers in sayings called the Beatitudes [“bee-AT-ih-toodz”], and he teaches a prayer that begins “Our Father, who art in heaven.”
tossups.r: That figure, Jesus of Nazareth, is believed by its followers to be the Son of God. For 10 points, name this religion.

tossups.p: The Coptic Church of Egypt and the Armenian Apostolic Church belong to the Oriental Orthodox churches of this religion, a family that rejected the decisions of the Council of Chalcedon [“KAL-suh-don”] in 451. This religion’s largest branch is led by the bishop of Rome, the pope.
tossups.r: With more than two billion followers, it is the largest religion on Earth. For 10 points, name this religion based on the life and teachings of Jesus.

tossups.p: In an Easter letter of 367 CE, Athanasius [“ath-uh-NAY-shus”] of Alexandria gave the earliest known list matching the twenty-seven books of this religion’s New Testament. Four of those books, traditionally credited to Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, tell of Jesus’s life and are called the Gospels, meaning “good news.”
tossups.r: Its Bible joins that New Testament to the Old Testament. For 10 points, name this religion that began with the followers of Jesus.

clues.t: Based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth, whom its followers believe to be the Son of God
Holy book: the Bible, made up of the Old Testament and the New Testament
Its followers believe Jesus was crucified and rose from the dead; the cross is its best-known symbol
Major holidays: Christmas (Jesus’s birth) and Easter (his resurrection)
The world’s largest religion, with more than two billion followers
Most branches teach the Trinity: one God in three persons, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit
Main branches: Roman Catholic (led by the pope), Eastern Orthodox, and Protestant
The Council of Nicaea (325), called by Constantine, condemned Arius, declared the Son “of the same substance” as the Father, and began the Nicene Creed
The Edict of Milan (313) allowed it to be practiced freely across the Roman Empire
The Great Schism (1054) split the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches
The Protestant Reformation began in 1517 with Martin Luther’s Ninety-five Theses
Catholics and Orthodox count seven sacraments; most Protestants count two, baptism and communion
In the Eucharist, or Holy Communion, believers share bread and wine, as Jesus did at the Last Supper
Four Gospels (“good news”), traditionally credited to Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John, tell of Jesus’s life
Acts says its believers first got their name at Antioch; the missionary Paul spread the faith among non-Jews
Lent, about forty days of prayer and fasting, begins on Ash Wednesday; Western churches usually hold Easter on the first Sunday after the first full moon of spring
Pliny the Younger asked Trajan how to deal with its followers (c. 112 CE); Tacitus wrote that Nero blamed them for Rome’s fire of 64 CE
Constantine reportedly marked his soldiers’ shields with the Chi-Rho before the Battle of the Milvian Bridge (312)
Schism disputes: the pope’s authority and the filioque (“and the Son”) added to the creed; Michael Cerularius was patriarch
The Council of Trent (1545–1563) and the Jesuits led the Catholic response to the Reformation
Ichthys, Greek for “fish,” was read as an acronym for “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Savior”
Tradition says Armenia became the first kingdom to make it official (301) after Gregory the Illuminator converted Tiridates III; Theodosius I made it Rome’s official religion in 380
Many Orthodox churches celebrate Christmas on January 7 (Julian calendar); Epiphany recalls the visit of the Magi
The Second Vatican Council (1962–1965) allowed Mass in local languages; Saint Jerome’s Latin translation is the Vulgate
In Matthew’s Great Commission, Jesus says to make disciples of all nations, baptizing in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit
Sermon on the Mount: the Beatitudes (“Blessed are the meek”) and the prayer that begins “Our Father”
Oriental Orthodox churches, such as the Coptic and Armenian churches, rejected the Council of Chalcedon (451)
Athanasius’s Easter letter of 367 CE gave the earliest known list matching the 27 books of the New Testament

trap.title: Whole faith, not one branch
trap.body: Many clues for this answer come from one part of its history, such as the pope, the Great Schism, or the Protestant Reformation. Naming a single branch, like Catholicism, Eastern Orthodoxy, or Protestantism, is wrong when the question asks for the whole religion. Judaism and Islam also honor Abraham and Moses, so an Old Testament clue alone is not enough.
trap.fix: If the question says “this religion” and its clues reach across eras or branches, answer Christianity (“Christians” also works). Jesus, the Trinity, the New Testament, Nicaea, Easter, or the cross point here. Save “Catholicism” or “Protestantism” for a question that asks for “this church” or “this branch.”
trap.line: Real answer line: Christianity (accept word forms like Christians; do not accept a single branch such as “Catholicism” or “Protestantism”)
